questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: How much packaging is needed for shipping.
Where items can be placed on the trailer.
How to load and unload the material.

questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. A material's hazard class shows what dangers it has.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, park at least ____ away from buildings.
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, stay at least 300 feet away from bridges, tunnels, and buildings. The only exception is parking for a short time during necessary tasks like refueling.

questions.question: Hazardous materials should be loaded and unloaded:
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials become more dangerous when exposed to heat. Always load and unload them away from heat sources.

questions.question: What does it mean if the Hazardous Materials Table says "Forbidden" in the third column?

options.text: Transport this substance only by air.
Transport this substance only at night.
Transport this substance with a security guard.

questions.explanation: The third column of the Hazardous Materials Table lists hazard classes and divisions. Never transport a material marked "Forbidden."

questions.question: If shipping papers say "Inhalation Hazard," which placard must the shipper provide?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If shipping papers or a package say "Inhalation Hazard," display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard as appropriate.

questions.question: When must you use a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard?

options.text: For any amount of the product.
Only when the container is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any amount of the product.
questions.explanation: For applicable materials, you must always display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard and the proper hazard class placard, even for small amounts.

questions.question: You may leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended:

options.text: On the side of a highway.

questions.explanation: You may leave your vehicle unattended only in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: A hazardous materials placard is shaped like a:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When loading or unloading explosives, you should:

options.text: Use sharp tools to open packages.

questions.explanation: Always turn off your engine before loading or unloading explosives. Never drop, throw, or roll packages with explosives.

questions.question: If you find a cargo leak, identify the materials using:
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Do not smell or touch leaking materials because this could cause injury or death.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, how should the trailer be cleaned?

options.text: Leave it to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: You must wash all vehicle parts exposed to corrosive liquids with water.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Load containers one at a time by hand. Keep them upright. Never drop or roll the containers.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put it out with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Hope the fire goes out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires require special training and protective gear. Do not try to fight these fires yourself unless you have proper equipment and training.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tire with your hand.
Measure how tall the tire is.

questions.explanation: Check your tires at the start of every trip and after each stop. A tire pressure gauge is the only correct way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: What type of hazardous material is Class 7?
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials are classified as Class 7 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Who is responsible for putting placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Shippers provide the placards, but the driver must install them on the vehicle.

questions.question: How are hazardous materials warnings displayed?

options.text: By wrapping the package in orange
By separating the item from other cargo and covering it with a sign

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on vehicles and bulk packages to warn others about hazardous materials.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The risks associated with the material
How fast the material must reach its destination

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are placed into nine classes to identify the type of risks they pose.

questions.question: Which agency performs a background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: You must pass a Transportation Security Administration (TSA) background check to get a new or renewed hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: Which agency coordinates emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.explanation: The National Response Center coordinates emergency response to chemical hazards and should be called if there is a hazardous materials spill.

questions.question: Opening trailer doors during a cargo fire can make the fire worse. Why?

options.text: It lets oxygen into the trailer.
It adds moisture to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets oxygen into the trailer.
questions.explanation: During a cargo fire, do not open the trailer doors. Opening them allows oxygen to enter, which makes the fire spread and get worse.

questions.question: You notice hazardous materials leaking from your vehicle while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to find a phone and call the National Response Center.
Leave the area to find help.

questions.explanation: If hazardous materials are leaking, park immediately. The longer you drive, the larger the contamination trail becomes. This increases danger to others and cleanup costs.

questions.question: Which incident does NOT require notification to the National Response Center?
questions.explanation: You must notify the National Response Center if there is death, hospitalization, $50,000 or more in property damage, evacuation of the public, or closure of a major route for more than one hour. You must also report fire, spillage, or contamination involving radiation, bacteria, or toxins. Report anything the carrier considers serious.

questions.question: Which location is NOT acceptable for keeping hazardous materials shipping papers?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while the seat belt is fastened.
On the driver's seat when the driver is outside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be in a pouch on the driver's door or within the driver's reach when driving. When the driver is outside the vehicle, papers should be on the driver's seat.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials cannot be transported in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Do not use heaters when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: If your vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, you should:

options.text: Not warn others about the danger.
Leave explosives in the vehicle until after separating the vehicles.
Remove explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.
questions.explanation: After a collision involving Class 1 explosives, warn others of danger and keep people away. Do not allow smoking or open fires. Remove the explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from vehicles and buildings before separating the vehicles.

questions.question: Which sign shows that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: Cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
Cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
Cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums are often used to store and transport hazardous materials. They can be a sign that the cargo is hazardous.

questions.question: While driving, where should shipping papers be kept?
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in another place you can reach easily while wearing your seat belt. Papers must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Shipping papers must include:
questions.explanation: Shippers must include an emergency response telephone number on all hazardous materials shipping papers.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare package markings and labels to shipping papers. Verify that the shipper used the correct description on the paper and placed proper labels on packages.
